notes.title: Life is Feudal: Arden - patch notes 0.27.0.46
notes.notes:
[p]Our main development focus remains on the "seasonal" system and critical bugs. While many of the upcoming changes are designed to bring forth the "seasonal" world, the team also works to address the current errors. Some of them are included in today's patch.[/p][h2][b]
Character progression[/b][/h2][p align="justify"][b]Fixed:[/b] the team has implemented a solution that should help with offline leveling. This bug has a very complex structure, so we will be closely monitoring the players’ feedback to evaluate the effectiveness of the solution. [/p][p][/p][p align="justify"]Unfortunately, the bug has already done the damage, preventing players from effectively levelling their skills and progressing in the game. We understand that the situation was extremely frustrating, and we apologize for the inconvenience the bug has brought to the feudals. [/p][p align="justify"]In order to help players reclaim time lost we will be launching [b]a compensation programme.[/b][/p][p align="justify"]In order to be eligible for the compensation, a player must be active in the game, meaning [b]their latest log in date should be no earlier than June 1st[/b]. Players who had contacted the support team about the bug outside this timeframe can reopen/create an inquiry and send the ID of their initial ticket - the decision on compensation will be taken case by case.[/p][p][/p][p align="justify"]We will be giving players the following items as compensation: [/p][list][*][p align="justify"]30 days of premium subscription for the players who could not use dual skilling as a part of their premium during the time the bug was active;[/p][/*][*][p align="justify"]14 days of premium subscription for the players without an active premium.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p align="justify"][b]We will launch the compensation process once we confirm that the fix is effective and the bug is no longer affect the players.[/b] [/p][p align="justify"]It might take some time before the compensation is delivered to all affected players, it might not appear in your account inventory right away. [/p][h2]
[b]Guilds[/b][/h2][p][b]New:[/b] Currently, players can only change personalities within their own monument or military outpost territory. To improve collaboration between allied guilds and enhance QoL for cooperative gameplay, players are now allowed to [b]change builds[/b] within territories of [b]friendly and allied monuments or military outposts[/b].[/p][h2]
[b]Map[/b][/h2][p align="justify"][b]Fixed:[/b] we corrected the text listing unique resources for each region - now it coincides 100% with the icons.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]UX/UI[/b][/h2][p align="justify"][b]Change:[/b] The legacy tech name of the Arden’s map (“Vulcan”) caused occasional confusion among players when they encountered it in-game. Therefore we have changed it to “Arden” everywhere players may interact with it.  [/p][p align="justify"][b]New:[/b] One of our goals is to implement additional instruments and provide new players with useful tips on how the LiF mechanics work. Calender tends to be confusing for the newcomers, that is why we have added special icons with pop-up instructions on how to utilize it. [/p][h2]

Technical issues[/h2][p][b]Fixed:[/b] a player no longer can apply poison for an unlimited number of times using a container.[/p][p][b]Fixed:[/b] NPCs on the newbie island no longer glow with blue light. [/p][p][b]Fixed:[/b] we have refreshed the newbie islands to prevent situations when a player could not complete a tutorial quest due to depletion of the world. We will also continue working on the tutorial, i.a. we plan to improve the quest line to give a better taste of the game.[/p][p][/p][p]This patch also contains an update for the anti-cheat software. The integration was successful, but players may still encounter minor difficulties while logging in to the game for the first time after the patch. We will closely monitor the situation - please do not hesitate to let our CM or support team know if you’re having troubles, we will be swift to address them.[/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Life is Feudal: Arden - patch notes 0.27.0.44
notes.notes:
[p]We are happy to present you with a new long-awaited patch. This time we doubled down on issues related to guild JHs and Arena. The patch also contains highly anticipated fixes and changes for some crafting structures. Here we go![/p][h2]
CHANGES[/h2][p][/p][h3]Guilds[/h3][p][b]Changed: [/b]Currently, low-rank guilds (typically ranks 8–10) are only subject to Judgment Hour (JH) on weekends. This system is being abused by players to create temporary "onion" claims – small, disposable guilds placed around valuable areas to exploit claim protection while avoiding regular JH exposure.[/p][p]To address this issue, the JH schedule will be adjusted so that all guilds, regardless of rank, [b]have at least one daily[/b] Judgment Hour (min 1h duration). This change promotes fairness, reduces abuse potential, and discourages exploitative claim layering tactics.[/p][p]The display of JH for guilds was adjusted to fit the new rule.[/p][p]We understand that it is a big change that will seriously affect the gameplay, esp. during the initial stages. We will monitor the situation in the game to see if the change needs further adjustments. [/p][p][b]New[/b]: guilds that own the province containing their own monument receive a bonus: both primary and secondary Judgment Hour (JH) durations are capped at 30 minutes. This bonus applies only while the guild controls its own province and is removed immediately if province ownership is lost.[/p][p]With this new mechanic we want to support experienced yet compact guilds, which have the capabilities to win in an IB, but may not have enough manpower to fend off an open-world JH attack, especially if the attacking side is represented by a group of overwhelmingly large forces.  [/p][p][/p][h3]Crafting[/h3][p][b]Changed:[/b] Large Herbal Garden now produces about 38-42 herbs at one time.[/p][h3]
Items and structures[/h3][p][b]Changed: [/b]“Blade Stand” is now a container (same as “Weapon Racks”) with 150 inventory capacity - it is possible to put weapons in it.[/p][h3]
[b]UX/UI[/b][/h3][p][b]Changed: [/b]the character’s window now includes visual indication of equipped items’ durability.[/p][p][/p][h2]
BUG FIXES[/h2][p][/p][h3]Character development[/h3][p][b]Fixed:[/b] occasionally a non-premium player could temporarily exceed the 500K exp.cap. This bug has now been fixed.[/p][p][/p][h3]Personal claims[/h3][p][b]Fixed:[/b] according to the rules, if a monument’s durability drops below 0, it will be destroyed (applies to all in-game structures). However, due to a bug, each time a monument’s durability approached the critical low, it would bounce back. This issue is now fixed, the monuments will disappear if their durability is depleted. This will help to automatically remove the abandoned claims and clear the space for active players.[/p][h3]
Crafting[/h3][p][b]Fixed:[/b] “Drying frames” – you no longer need to have a stack of 10 skins in your inventory to initiate the process.[/p][h3]
Guilds[/h3][p][b]Fixed[/b]: if a guild in timezone A builds a military outpost in timezone B, it will be offered to set the JH slots for the MOP in timeframe local to timezone B. This was a part of the initial outposts mechanics design, and we are happy that it is now fully realized in the game. [/p][p][b]Fixed:[/b] now the surezains are displayed correctly for the vassal guilds.[/p][p][b]Fixed:[/b] previously if a guild A had several vassals (A1, A2, A3), and a guild B declared war on the guild A, only one of the vassals (ex.A1) switched to “in war” with guild B (guilds A2 and A3 remained neutral). Now this applies to all vassals of a guild. [/p][h3]
Arena[/h3][p][b]Fixed: [/b]we have improved arena matchmaking protocol, so now the players won’t risk being split if several parties register for the arena. We also fixed the issue when a player could be stuck with a grayed-out “join arena” button if their assigned duel counterpart left the queue. [/p][p][/p][h3]Technical[/h3][p][b]Fixed: [/b]some players encountered an issue when they could not see their characters in their account, even though they used the correct authentication method. With this patch, we introduced a correction that should resolve the matter. We will be listening closely to the feedback from the affected players. We apologize for the inconvenience this situation has been causing you.[/p][p]Players who could not use the benefits associated with Premium subscription will be contacted by our support team to arrange compensation.[/p][p][b]Fixed:[/b] the in-game link to the official Discord server now works properly. 
[/p][p]We have also introduced new fixes to improve server stability. [/p][p][/p][h3]Shop and cosmetics[/h3][p][b]Fixed: [/b]we have made a comprehensive revision of the items sold in the in-game shop. Now all armor/clothes for torso should go as “skins” for a corresponding in-game item. We also have fixed the durability of the “Believer’s cooking pot”. [/p][p][b]Fixed: [/b]“Elegant Purple Cloak” is now a skin that can be applied to “Rags”. Some players wore them as tabards above the armor, which created confusion during battle. We also received reports that players could occasionally destroy the cloak by mistake. In the light of those factors we decided to convert the item to a skin.[/p][p][/p][h2]Next steps[/h2][p]Following your feedback, we continue to finetune the JH mechanics to make them more engaging and balanced, and also to tackle the existing detrimental schemes such as “onion claims”. It is a continuous process and a complicated balancing act that requires trial and error. We will analyse the effects these changes on the game world and inter-guild relations to see if they align with our vision for the desired gameplay experience.
[/p][p]The team is currently working hard to facilitate the advance of the seasonal model and ensure that this transition is as seamless as possible. We are especially focused on preparing the game for the launch of Season 1, which will mark a new chapter in Life is Feudal and introduce a fresh competitive and progression-oriented structure to the game.[/p][p][/p][p]We are also ready to announce that players can expect a new cosmetics system in the near future. Although this update was previously postponed due to shifting priorities, the team is now fully committed to releasing it. The new cosmetics will not only enhance the visual style of Life is Feudal but will also introduce new types of interactions between players.[/p][p]




[/p][p]

[/p][h3][/h3]

notes.title: Developers' Stream 19/06/2025 - Text Version
notes.notes:
[h2][b]Why introduce "Seasons" at all? Were other options considered? Were you inspired by other games?[/b][/h2][p]We’ve studied how sandbox games naturally follow a lifespan curve – initial excitement, then a slow decline without fresh incentives. "Seasons" are our way of keeping the experience dynamic and engaging. They offer:[/p][list][*][p][b]Structured progression[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Phased unlocks[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Varied goals[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Time-limited competition with real rewards[/b][/p][/*][/list][p]We didn’t want to just "wipe and restart". Instead, each "Season" is a [b]curated experience[/b], inspired by successful systems in [b]Rust[/b], [b]Albion Online[/b], and [b]Path of Exile[/b].[/p][p]We still believe in the value of a [b]persistent world[/b], like Goldenland. But we’ve also learned that truly permanent servers often lead to stagnation, imbalance, and burnout – especially once a few groups dominate. "[b]Seasonal" worlds[/b] give us space to experiment, reset, and deliver meaningful change without breaking the core of what Life is Feudal stands for.[/p][p]The dual-world model (persistent PvE and seasonal PvP) gives players a real choice in how they want to experience Arden – and we think that’s the best path forward.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Can you tell us more about the mechanic of gradual unlocking of buildings and recipes that you’ve already announced as a main feature for the first "Season"?[/b][/h2][p]Each “Season” is divided into “Ages,” with each Age lasting around 4 weeks. As the "Season" progresses, new "Ages" unlock more content – including buildings, crafting recipes, gear tiers, and bonuses. This phased progression helps maintain game balance and gives everyone a fair chance to catch up and compete.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Will you release a list of unlocked structures at the beginning of every "Age"?[/b][/h2][p]Yes! You’ll be able to see the list of available and upcoming unlocks directly in the game via the seasonal UI. It will show what’s currently accessible and what’s coming next in each "Age", so you can plan your progression without needing to check outside sources.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Are there any progression bonuses during the "Season"?[/b][/h2][p]Yes, there are stacking progression bonuses as the "Season" unfolds. These include things like:[/p][list][*][p]Increased wood and crop yields[/p][/*][*][p]Miner’s bonuses and faster blacksmith crafting[/p][/*][*][p]Better animal spawns and breeding rates[/p][/*][*][p]XP boosts to help late joiners catch up[/p][/*][*][p]Increased PvP damage during the final month
[/p][/*][/list][h2][b]LiF is designed for a slow-paced progression. What changes will be needed in mechanics to transform the LiF gameplay into “seasonal”?[/b][/h2][p]You're absolutely right – Life is Feudal was originally built around long-term, persistent progression. To adapt it to a seasonal format, we’re rebalancing some crafting requirements and skill dependencies to better match the faster pacing. The idea is to maintain the depth and meaning of progression, without making it feel like a grind that doesn’t pay off in time.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Given a “Season” is only 6 months, will crafting and leveling rates be adjusted accordingly? [/b][/h2][p]Yes. Skill progression – especially offline leveling for higher-tier skills (like T4) – will be adjusted based on when those skills become available in the "Age" system. We don’t want players spending weeks leveling something they can’t even use yet. We've also tuned XP gain to reward consistent, active play, rather than grindy rushes. Additionally, tree growth, wild seed quality, and animal quality have all been improved to help players progress into high-end farming and breeding faster – all in sync with the 6-month "season" structure.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Are “Seasons” changing the core of Life is Feudal?[/b][/h2][p]Not at all. “Seasons” aren’t about turning Life is Feudal into a different game – they’re about offering new ways to enjoy the same game. It’s a more focused, time-limited experience that complements the persistent world. We’re still actively maintaining and improving the core systems for players who prefer that long-term playstyle.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]In the original dev blog about “Seasons,” it was mentioned that the world would be wiped after each cycle. This raised concerns, especially among PvE players. Has the team come up with a way to preserve the long-term, persistent nature of Life is Feudal alongside the new seasonal model?[/b][/h2][p]Yes – for the first “Season” we’ve introduced a dual-world structure to support both playstyles.[/p][list][*][p][b]Arden ("green zone")[/b] will remain a persistent PvE world. All your characters, stats, gear, and private claims will be preserved there, with no "seasonal" wipes. This world is focused on long-term building, crafting, and cooperative gameplay.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Seasonal Arden ("red zone")[/b] is a competitive PvP world with structured seasonal resets and progression phases. It’s designed for those who enjoy fresh starts, competitive goals, and a more intense, time-limited experience.[/p][/*][/list][p]By running both worlds in parallel, we can tailor mechanics like wipe schedules, durability loss, trading, and progression speed to fit each playstyle – without compromising the core identity of the game.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]So does that mean it will be like choosing a world every time we log in – but now with three options: “Newbie Island”, Arden ("green zone"), and Seasonal Arden ("red zone")? [/b][/h2][p]Yes, exactly. With the start of the first "Season" and the "red zone" wipe, all current player characters will be moved to the persistent Arden "green zone" (private claim area). From there, you’ll get to choose one of three transfer options, depending on your playstyle and guild status:[/p][olist][*][p][b]Join "guilds green zone":[/b] Your character joins a designated guild settlement in the ex red zone Arden that becomes PVE Guild zone, unlocking full guild claim building without JHs.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Remain in legacy "green zone":[/b] Your character stays on your existing private claim in the classic "green zone".[/p][/*][*][p][b]Transfer to Seasonal Arden ("red zone"):[/b] Your character moves to the new "seasonal" PvP world, which triggers a full "seasonal" reset. [/p][/*][/olist][p]This transfer process is initiated when you interact with either the “Seasonal Ferryman” (new) or the traditional “Ferryman” (for legacy migration).[/p][p]While it’s not a 1:1 copy of Avalon and Epleland, this setup is their spiritual successor — providing a clear separation between PvE and PvP worlds, each with its own systems and priorities.[/p][p]The seasonal "red zone" map intentionally has no "green zone"— it’s focused entirely on competitive, time-limited PvP. A full wipe happens every "Season" in the RedZone, including character data, buildings, terraforming, inventories, guild claims, and even the world generation. The "red zone" also uses the "Age" system for phased unlocks and "seasonal" modifiers, offering a fresh, challenging experience every 6 months.[/p][p][/p][h1][b]Do we understand correctly that the current Arden "green zone" will not be wiped – not during the transition to "Seasons", and not in the foreseeable future? And that it’s even expanding into what used to be "red zone" territory?[/b][/h1][p]Yes, that’s correct! The Arden "green zone" for private claims will remain persistent – no wipe during the first "Season" launch or in the foreseeable future.  In fact, we’re expanding its territory into areas that were previously part of the "red zone". Actual "red zone" terrains will be wiped to convert into "green zone" for guild claim so PvE-focused groups can enjoy organized group play without being pushed into "seasonal" wipes or siege PvP environments.  We do not plan to do wipe on both areas just to wipe them.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Will PvP be completely disabled in Arden "green zone", or will there be exceptions?[/b][/h2][p]That’s still under internal discussion. What we can say for sure is:[/p][list][*][p][b]Seasonal Arden ("red zone")[/b] will be full PvP with no restrictions.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Current "green zone" [/b]will remain fully PvE.[/p][/*][*][p][b]"Guild green zone" [/b]designed more for long-term guild development and PvE-friendly play without JHs.[/p][/*][/list][p]Whether or not "guild green zone" will allow some limited or situational open-world PvP is something we’re still considering – and we’d really love to hear what the community thinks about it![/p][p][/p][h2][b]Will it be possible to migrate between the two worlds – "green zone" and Seasonal Arden?[/b][/h2][p]Yes, migration between worlds will be possible. However, transferring from [b]"green zone" (PvE)[/b] to [b]Seasonal Arden (PvP)[/b] will trigger a [b]reset effect[/b] to maintain fairness and competitive balance in the "seasonal" environment.[/p][p]Here’s how the reset works when moving into Seasonal Arden:[/p][list][*][p][b]Stats are capped[/b] (35 to 20)[/p][/*][*][p][b]Combat and crafting skills are scaled down[/b][/p][list][*][p]T1 → 60[/p][/*][*][p]T2 → 30[/p][/*][*][p]T3–T4 → 0[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Inventory is wiped[/b], except for no-drop (bound) items[/p][/*][/list][p]This ensures everyone starts the first "Season" on equal footing.[/p][p]On the flip side, if you transfer a character [b]from PvP back to PvE[/b], your progress will not be reset. That said, we are actively monitoring this system and may introduce cooldowns or tighter restrictions in the future if it’s necessary to prevent any kind of exploitation.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]When do you plan the wipe and the launch of the first "Season"?[/b][/h2][p]We’re aiming to launch the first full "seasonal" wipe and first "[b]Season"[/b] [b]late summer to early autumn[/b].[/p][p]The exact timing will depend on final testing and server preparation. We’ll make sure to keep players updated on all key milestones along the way, so you’ll have enough time to plan your gameplay and migration in advance.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]If I understand correctly, the next Arden "red zone" wipe will happen about 6 months after the first "Season" starts. Will "Seasons" always last exactly 6 months? Can they be longer? What will the length of a "Season" depend on?[/b][/h2][p]You’re right – the current plan is for each "Season" to last [b]about 6 months[/b]. That gives players enough time to build up, engage in PvP, and hit meaningful milestones without rushing.[/p][p]However, the 6-month cycle isn’t set in stone. "Season" length may change in the future depending on:[/p][list][*][p][b]Player feedback[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Activity levels throughout the "Season"[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]How quickly players complete "seasonal" content[/b][/p][/*][/list][p]So yes, some "Seasons" might be a bit shorter or longer – we’ll stay flexible to make sure each one feels fresh and rewarding.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Despite all the new features, Life is Feudal still focuses on guild-vs-guild conflict. With "Seasons", that seems even more important, as guilds will be competing for rankings and rewards. Can you tell us more about how that will work?[/b][/h2][p]Yes – guild competition is at the heart of the "seasonal" experience. Each "Season" will include specific goals and scoring metrics tied to things like [b]war score[/b], [b]territory control[/b], [b]guild wealth[/b], and [b]social influence[/b].[/p][p]Guilds will earn [b]seasonal points[/b] through:[/p][list][*][p]Winning [b]Instanced Battles (IBs)[/b][/p][/*][*][p]Accumulating [b]wealth and guild rank[/b][/p][/*][*][p]Controlling [b]provinces[/b] at the end of the Season[/p][/*][/list][p]We’re also working on a [b]seasonal leaderboard or achievement board[/b] to help players track their progress and compare standings. While we can’t guarantee it’ll be ready in time for first "Season" due to technical factors, it’s definitely something we plan to introduce in future updates.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]If one of the "seasonal" objectives is to claim the most provinces, won’t the NA region be at a disadvantage due to having fewer provinces?[/b][/h2][p]Yes, we’re aware of that imbalance. We’re currently reviewing province distribution and how scoring is calculated to ensure that regions like NA aren’t at a structural disadvantage when it comes to territory-based objectives. Fairness across regions is a key focus.[/p][h2][/h2][h2][b]Will the rules for Instanced Battles (IBs) be reworked so only the attacker and defender guild members can participate, without random “free swords”?[/b][/h2][p]We’re actively exploring that. One idea on the table is a [b]sign-up system[/b] tied to the guild’s [b]monument or totem[/b], where only members of the attacking and defending guilds (and possibly their formal allies) would be able to join. The goal is to prevent random, unaffiliated players from joining IBs and undermining the structure.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]What changes were made to the guild system in preparation for "Seasons"?[/b][/h2][p]Several important updates were introduced:[/p][list][*][p][b]Guilds are now limited to 50 unique accounts (100 characters)[/b] – this encourages tighter coordination and helps reduce zerging and mega-alliances.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Friendly/Ally access to guild objects is disabled[/b] – guilds can no longer give shared access to buildings and resources.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Sharing between guilds and personal characters is suspended[/b] – this makes it harder to bypass mechanics using alts or “onion-claim” layering.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Internal ranks and permissions within a single guild still work as before[/b], so structured hierarchies and role management remain fully supported.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h2][b]How do you plan to balance small and large guilds during "Seasons"?[/b][/h2][p]We want "Seasons" to be rewarding for both large alliances and smaller groups. To support that, we’re introducing age-based progression limits, which prevent large guilds from rushing straight to endgame content early in the "Season".[/p][p]We’re also considering mentorship and cooperation mechanics in future updates to help smaller groups grow and stay competitive throughout the "seasonal" cycle.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Some players are unhappy with the limits on asset sharing. Why was this decision made, and are there any alternatives being considered? [/b][/h2][p]We totally understand the frustration – it wasn’t an easy call. These restrictions were introduced to curb serious abuse of alliance mechanics, like hidden ownership, tax loopholes, and ways to bypass siege mechanics using alt guilds.[/p][p]Long-term, we [b]do[/b] want to bring back alliance systems, but in a [b]cleaner, more structured form[/b] that enables cooperation without allowing exploits. We also want to promote local wars.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]If I’m in the same guild as someone, can I still lose alignment for friendly fire?[/b][/h2][p]No – if you and your ally are in the [b]same guild[/b], you [b]won’t lose alignment[/b] for accidental hits. Alignment loss applies mainly when you attack innocent or neutral players [b]outside[/b] your guild.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Doesn’t this change kill player-led hubs like “Jita City”? Can there be exceptions?[/b][/h2][p]We deeply value community-driven projects like [i]Jita City[/i]. While current changes limit asset sharing for balance reasons, we’re actively discussing ways to support [b]trusted public initiatives[/b] in the future – possibly through [b]dedicated permissions[/b], [b]shared zones[/b], or [b]special player roles[/b].[/p][p]That said, [b]in the Arden "green zone" (PvE)[/b] – especially in the [b]guild-supporting regions[/b] – you’ll still be able to build [b]similar community hubs[/b] without the pressure of PvP or "seasonal" resets. It’s a great place for long-term, cooperative projects to thrive freely, outside of the competitive "seasonal" cycle.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Do you plan to add more ways to make money for upkeep? Will upkeep costs be further adjusted? Is the system effective against the “onion” claim strategy?[/b][/h2][p]Yes – we’re planning to introduce more coin generation methods, especially to support smaller or PvE-oriented groups. We’re also open to further tuning upkeep costs based on [b]territory size[/b], [b]claim value[/b], and [b]player activity[/b].[/p][p]We know that the current system can sometimes punish successful conquest by increasing upkeep on newly claimed outposts – and that it hasn’t fully solved the problem of “onion” claim abuse. These issues are under active review as we tune Season 1, and your feedback is a big part of that process.[/p][p][/p][h2]Do you have any plans to rebalance PvP, make it smoother?[/h2][p]There are a lot of factors that go into this topic- balancing not only weapons, but armors, desync, lags. In a way, that is a never-ending, perpetual project. Some of the factors are much harder to change than others, but there are definitely plans to rebalance weapons and armors. These changes may not come fast, but the research on how to make the combat better is underway.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Let’s talk about rewards! What can top guilds expect at the end of the Season?[/b][/h2][p]Top-performing guilds will receive unique [b]seasonal titles[/b], like [i]“Royal Guild,”[/i] and [b]cosmetic rewards[/b] such as customised guild banners.[/p][p]Looking ahead, we’re planning [b]customizable guild objects[/b] – flags, statues, decorative monuments – that give top guilds a lasting, visible presence across "Sseasons". These will serve as both bragging rights and legacy markers in the world.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]The "seasonal" model sounds ambitious. Will the dev team really be able to keep up with the pace of updates and new content?[/b][/h2][p]That’s a fair concern, and yes – the goal behind the "seasonal" model is to establish a [b]more sustainable and predictable development cycle[/b]. Instead of patching the persistent world indefinitely, "Seasons" give us natural windows to [b]test, refine, and release content[/b] in sync with each phase.[/p][p]This approach helps reduce bugs, improve feature stability, and avoid mid-season disruptions. We're not aiming to deliver everything at once – but seasonal pacing lets us build, ship, and improve in more focused cycles.[/p][p]"Seasonal" approach also helps us manage the database strain and improve performance, as each "Season" the players will be starting from a clean sheet without the accumulated clutter. We know about the ping problems and packet loss, the team continues to work on them, it is actually one of our top priorities. Although we are constrained with the instruments available, we continue to search for the solutions, and we are determined to succeed.[/p][p]We also want to specify that the server structure is completely different from what it was, so the current hardware does not act as a limiting factor for performance. We have a very good DevOps team, which experiments with hardware and works towards the best possible state of the game.[/p][p]Lag compensation system is something we need to reinvent. Unlike Unity of UE5, the current game client does not offer a satisfactory out-of-the-box option. The current LiF version is on the older side. However, we experimented with switching it off, and received feedback from players that the situation got worse. We currently have lag compensation on for arenas and IBs, but for the open world PvP it is off. According to the feedback and to our research, it is as optimal as can be for the current moment.[/p][h3]And no, the bubble does not exist ;)[/h3][p]The model has meshes and collusions. Let’s illustrate it with an example. Sometimes you cannot pass behind the horse as if there was a ghost behind it. It is caused by a desynch. Your client is sending packets to the server, the server is sending packets to your client. If there is too much packets, it creates a bottleneck, so your game might be delayed compared to the server. The horse on your screen may not be in the place where server puts it. We are working on optimization of connection and models to make it smoother. [/p][p][/p][h2][b]Will we see new maps in future "Seasons"? Can each "Season" have a unique world?[/b][/h2][p]Technically, yes – it's [b]possible to introduce new maps[/b] with each "Season", and we’re strongly considering it for the future.[/p][p]However, for first "[b]Season"[/b], we’re sticking with the [b]current map[/b]. Our immediate priority is stability, core system polish, and balanced gameplay. Once that foundation is in place, we’ll have more room to expand with dynamic terrain layouts and experimental designs.[/p][p]Of course, the underground resources will be regenerated. We also know about the underground rock problem and will try to address it.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Speaking of that – what’s the future of Godenland? Will it be further optimized, and can it become the main “perpetual” world now that Arden is moving to a seasonal model? [/b][/h2][p]Godenland will continue to serve as our no-wipe, no-season world – it’s the home for players who prefer long-term, persistent progression. While Arden offers a more structured and faster-paced "seasonal" experience, it doesn’t replace Godenland. Instead, both worlds are meant to coexist, each supporting a different playstyle.[/p][p]With the launch of first "Season", we will have three active worlds:[/p][list][*][p]Godenland[/p][/*][*][p]Arden ("green zone" private claims and guild claims, PvE)[/p][/*][*][p]Seasonal Arden ("red zone", PvP)[/p][/*][/list][p]Arden will receive all the same content updates as Seasonal Arden, ensuring feature parity and allowing PvE players to enjoy the same new systems, items, and improvements — just without "seasonal" wipes or PvP pressure.[/p][p]We also plan to optimize and maintain Godenland, keeping it a viable home for players who value continuity, deep settlement building, and long-term social development. Arden is more condensed and competitive, while Godenland is all about scale and staying power.[/p][p]So no, Arden won’t "replace" Godenland – it simply offers a different path through the same world.[/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: Life is Feudal: Arden - patch notes 0.27.0.38
notes.notes:
Feudals,
please see below a list of changes and fixes that got implemented during today's hotfix:

[h2]Animal lore[/h2]
[b]Fixed[/b]: calendar now fully displays “Harvest” for farming and animals.

[b]"Off-season breeding"[/b]
We have slightly reworked the new “off-season breeding” mechanic for animals, and now the quality increase is within the old parameters.
At the same time, animals can now breed during “off-season” days, but with reduced chance. Also “off-season” borned animals get slightly less chance to be better quality.
This change is needed to better balance the speed of quality progression for animals within the timeframe of the upcoming Seasons. 

[h2]Judgement hours (JH)[/h2]
[b]Fixed[/b]: the ability to “Get horse” now active only during the HJH for attackers. You would not be able to steal horses from the enemy’s stables during the JH.

[h2]Combat
[/h2]
[b]Changed[/b]: scope for bows was improved to increase convenience.
[b]Fixed[/b]: you can climb simple siege ladders again.

[h2]Shop
[/h2]
[b]Fixed[/b]: all instruments from the game shop have 125 durability and 50q. Previously purchased tools were swapped for the new ones.

[h2]Titles[/h2]
We made a promise to give special titles to the LiF’s most loyal fans. However, while working on this task, we discovered an issue that prevented correct attribution for the titles. Now the problem with the title system have finally been resolved, and players will be able to showcase their achievements in the future. We apologize for the delay and appreciate your patience!

Pre-LTG players of Life is Feudal received the title of “The Ancestor”
Pre-Steam players of Life is Feudal received the title of “The Prophet”

We hope that noone worthy of this title was left out, and you will wear them with pride!

This fix also enables us to provide titles promised in the Early Access packs. We hope that the players will be able to use all of their titles no later than next week. 

[h2]More on the “Seasons”:
[/h2]As the new “seasonal” system was announced, we have received a lot of feedback on what concerns the players,  what new elements the community would love to see in the game, and also - what elements people would prefer to keep unchanged. After internal discussion, the team set out to work on a version of a seasonal world where at least a part of the current Arden remains preserved. Although a full wipe would be easier to implement, we believe that the LiF spirit that enables a variety of gameplay styles is what makes the game so special and unique. Therefore, we are willing to make an effort and keep the space for players that prefer a little more perpetuity. 

We continue to collect your questions for the upcoming dev.stream. Hopefully next week we will be able to go live and share with you the complete vision for the future!

notes.title: Life is Feudal: Arden - patch notes 0.27.0.36
notes.notes:
[h1]Feudals,[/h1]
the patch contains some big changes and fixes. It also sets us up for transition to a new gameplay direction. Let's begin!
[h2]Guilds[/h2]
[b]Fixed:[/b] In order to maintain a guild monument on Arden, you  need to have at least 5 premium characters as members - otherwise a monument will collapse in 72 hours. However, this mechanic did not work properly, so we had several reports of guilds having less than 5 premium characters without any consequences. Now this issue has been fixed, and the mechanic will work as designed.

In conjunction with this, we would also like to announce that [b]the minimal number of characters with premium in a guild is decreased from 5 to 3![/b]

[b]Changed:[/b] upkeep for extra outposts will be increased.
Due to the absence of a limit on outposts for Tier 4 monuments, players have been able to construct and maintain almost unlimited number of outposts. The current situation makes claims more protected, as guilds can maintain multiple layers of outposts without significant upkeep consequences. By introducing a scaling upkeep system, we aim to create a strategic decision-making process where guilds must weigh the cost of additional outposts against their benefits.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342560/a6d5b5d5f6b9e603805743e9ee9ad0ae42b4e179.png[/img]
[b]How will it work?[/b]
[list]
[*] An increased upkeep multiplier will be applied to guilds with 8+ non-military outposts;
[*] Military outposts will not count towards the total number of outposts for this calculation;
[*] This change applies globally to all non-military outposts owned by a guild.[/list] [h2]Crafting[/h2]
[b]Changed:[/b] now the crafting structures will have a list of available recipes. In the “Craft” ability window you will see a “Recipies” button, which will show you all the items you can create with this structure, along with the materials required. For now, this function is enabled for “Big Drying Frame/ Drying Frame” and “Big Tanning Tub/ Tanning Tub”, but it will be expanded in the future patches.  
[b]N.B.[/b] You can experience an issue with indication of hides in a Drying Frame.
In this window, the indication will start from 10 hides, but you will only need 1 hide. However, you need to have 10 hides in inventory to launch the process. This is a known issue which will be addressed in our upcoming patches. 

[b]Changed:[/b] "Load of" ability has been adjusted. 
Reduced required resources: 
[list]
[*] Load of Charcoal: quantity 12->10
[*] Load of Linen hanks: quantity 55->50
[*] Load of Glass: quantity 22->20[/list] Increased required skill level:
[list]
[*] Load of Charcoal: skill 60->90
[*] Load of Linen hanks: skill 60->90
[*] Load of Glass: skill 60->90[/list] [h2]Animal lore[/h2]
[h3]Introducing “off-season” breeding for animals[/h3]
[b]New: [/b] we’re introducing a new off-season breeding system for animals. Even if an animal is not listed in the current in-game calendar week, it can still provide offsprings.
Animals that are “in-season” (as defined by the calendar) will receive full breeding bonuses, including quality increase. “Off-season” animals can now also breed during those days, but with reduced quality bonuses.
This gives players more flexibility in managing livestock, while still rewarding optimal timing based on the calendar. 
Let us illustrate the change with an example. The game currently has 6 different types of breedable animals: rabbit, chicken pig, sheep, cow, horse. If we look at the actual game calendar, on day 5 the animals which can breed are chicken, pig, cow - they are “in-season”. We want to make it so that the rest of the animals can also breed on day 5. However, the quality increase for off-searon animals will be lower: 
[list]
[*] Breeding animals “in-season”: chance to increase newborn quality by 1-4 points 
[*] Breeding animals “off-season”: chance to increase newborn quality by 1-2 points
[/list] [h2]Map[/h2]
[b]Fixed:[/b] the map’s regions filter now displays Arden’s regions.
[b]Fixed: [/b] new regions and new prime times are added to the map and the dashboard. [h2]Arenda/IBs[/h2]
[b]Fixed: [/b] Sometimes players might have encountered a “DB error” when attempting to teleport to an IB. Now the issue should be solved. [h2]Combat[/h2]
[b]Changes: [/b]Naphtha pot damage is reduced by 20%.
[b]New:[/b] fast-looting for corpses is now incorporated in LiF (Ctrl+LMB) and available for all players. We believe that this will help create a level-playing field in the long run. We will continue our work to combat third-party scripts which we find detrimental to the game. However, it is a delicate work, as we do not want to bash innocent players. [h2]Knools[/h2]
[b]Changed:[/b] the natives’ combat style is too archaic to challenge the feudals, a simple footwork, a step back could make them miss. But the natives learn, too. “Native Bear”, “Native Mole”, “Native Chieftain” will now come closer to the players and be more aggressive in their attacks. We will continue to work on knolls AI to make the encounters more interesting. [h2]Technical[/h2]
We continue to implement technical improvements so that the players never encounter “Waiting for server” error.[h2]UX/UI[/h2]
[b]Fixed: [/b] slider in “Battles” now lets players scroll down to see all the available IBs.
Various visual improvements, i.a. better “quality” depiction for some items.
[h2]What's next?[/h2]
This time, we would also like to give you a little peek at what is coming. Keep in mind that it is not an exhaustive list of tasks we set for ourselves. However, we believe that it outlines the key directions of work quite well. Hope you like it! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342560/778a16a0a961f15b604884f744fb8cf8bdabe137.png[/img]

notes.title: Life is feudal: Arden - Patch Notes 0.27.0.33
notes.notes:
Feudals,

With patch 0.27.0.33, we’ve rolled out a number of important fixes and updates that directly address community feedback and ongoing concerns. These changes are aimed at improving your overall gameplay experience and ensuring a smoother, more balanced adventure in the world of Life is Feudal.

[h3]Character progression[/h3]
[b]Fixed:[/b] We received many reports from players that said that their skills would stop growing/decreasing passively after they disconnect. The team has conducted a thorough research and identified the roots of the problem. It appears that one personality could influence the progress in another, for example if a player did not have the skill “Knight” unlocked for personality 1 (the icon displayed as gray, the preceding skill “Cavalry” had 29 points in it), this fact will stall the same skill on personality two (despite setting skill “Knight” to increase, the process will halt once a player disconnects).This issue has been fixed, now a skill should increase/decrease regardless of its status for different personalities. 
[b]Fixed:[/b] The available experience pool will now display correctly after a character loses a portion of it upon death.

[h3]Personal claims[/h3]
[b]Fixed:[/b] There were instances when a player could place two personal claims on the same account on different servers. This bug was fixed.
[b]Changed:[/b] Max size of a private claim was increased by 50% from 300 to 450 tiles. 

[h3]Guilds[/h3]
[b]Added:[/b] Now when guild A changes status with guild B to “Ally”, all players of guild B will receive a notification in the system chat. 
[b]Added:[/b] If a player tries to interact with support points of an outpost of an enemy guild, they will now receive a notification that this action is not possible.

[h3]Arena[/h3]
[b]Fixed:[/b] “Intellect” and “Constitution” stats no longer switch upon entering Arena/IB.

[h3]Knools[/h3]
[b]Added:[/b] The knools can now inflict “wounds” and “broken bones” statuses upon attack.

[h3]Crafting[/h3]
[b]Fixed:[/b] Regionality of resources, blueprints and items has been restored.
[b]Changed:[/b] To craft a “tabard”, one now needs 1 simple cloth instead of 1 linen cloth.

[h3]Hunting[/h3]
[b]Fixed:[/b] The ability “Look for tracks of peaceful animals/ tracks aggressive animals” sometimes required a character to receive damage from an animal to work properly. Now this issue is resolved.
[b]Fixed:[/b] We have further improved the tracking system so that the animal’s tracks are displayed properly.

[h3]Animal lore[/h3]
[b]Fixed:[/b] After the stable capacity increase, there was an issue that the maximum food and water storage does not scale properly with the new animal capacity. This issue has now been fixed: “Small Stables” now hold 360 stones of food, “Large Stables” hold 1200 stones of food, both with animals slots filled to maximum.
[b]Fixed:[/b] We have improved the calculation of quality for eggs in the “Coop”. Now it is possible to get 100q eggs with 100q chickens.

[h3]Technical[/h3]
[b]Fixed:[/b] When using the "Repair" ability, if both the item to repair and the repair kit are stored within inventory containers (e.g., storage box, backpack, sack), the repair kit is not consumed. This issue has now been fixed.
[b]Fixed:[/b] Lamp posts will now remember their last state and will remain lit even after maintenance or a server reboot.
[b]Fixed:[/b] Net event traffic optimized to reduce lag and desync.
[b]Changed:[/b] If player A launched interaction with an object via the “ability planning”, player B can no longer interact with the same object. For example, if player A is in the process of “Unharnessing” a cart, another player cannot interact with the same cart.

[h3]UX/UI[/h3]
[b]Fixed:[/b] Now if a player has more than 5 buffs and the “Enable window auto-adjust” is on, the description of buffs is displayed properly without it being cut
[b]Changed:[/b] We have adjusted the crosshair for ranged weapons to better reflect the projectile’s trajectory.
[b]Changed:[/b] Localization for certain actions has been updated

Thanks for sticking with us and sharing your thoughts — it really helps us make Life is Feudal better for everyone. We’ve got more fixes, tweaks, and changes in the works, so stay tuned!

notes.title: Life is Feudal: Arden - Patch Notes 0.27.0.29
notes.notes:
Feudals,

This patch brings several key improvements to both the game’s performance and overall player experience. One of the long-awaited features is already in place – Instanced Battles are finally launching in Arden! Players can now conquer provinces through intense 25v25 or 50v50 battles. It's time to rally your warriors, sharpen your pikes, pick the sturdiest shields, and prepare for battle – only the strongest will prevail! 

But there's more to come, as our focus is on optimizing performance and refining key aspects of the game to ensure a smoother experience, with even more enhancements coming in the future. Let’s go over all the details together:

[h3]Features[/h3]
[b]Changed[/b]: With this update, Instance Battles (IB) are now enabled. To launch them you’ll need a Battle Totem, as before.
Together with that, the provinces that were previously captured by the guilds during the time when IBs were not fully enabled have been cleared of their owners and are now unclaimed.
 
[h3]Character progression[/h3]
[b]Fixed[/b]: The issue with leveling skills with a skill cap has been resolved, and it now works correctly for any personality in the Combat skills tree.
[b]Fixed[/b]: The skill point redistribution now works as intended during passive leveling and remains effective upon re-logging. 

[h3]Bugfixes[/h3]
[b]Fixed[/b]: The account inventory has been optimized, ensuring that boosters in the pack activate correctly upon consumption.
[b]Fixed[/b]: The vulnerability that allowed players to duplicate items in trading posts was addressed.
[b]Fixed[/b]: The chance to lose maximum durability when using the repair ability now aligns with the specified values: a 3% durability decrease with Repair Kits and a 7% decrease for jewelry. This aspect was missed during the preparation of Arden, and the change has been implemented as we see a lot of items appearing in storages again. 
At the same time, repairing with a workbench does not lower durability.
[b]Fixed[/b]:  The issue with uploading files in the game client has been addressed, with the terrains being properly installed.
[b]Fixed[/b]: Decorator's Kit packs purchased in the store now unpack correctly when consumed, with the items being added to the player's inventory.
[b]Fixed[/b]: Adjustments have been made to the localization to refine certain phrasings.
[b]Fixed[/b]: Adjustments have been implemented to enhance server stability.

[h3]Farming[/h3]
[b]Fixed[/b]: The maximum number of plants that can be grown in the Large Herbal Garden has been increased to 85. Players can now plant more herbs at one time.

[h3]Character Abilities[/h3]
[b]Fixed[/b]: To prevent abuses, a 120-minute cooldown has been implemented for the /prayfor ability per account, persisting even if a character is deleted and recreated. 
[b]Fixed[/b]: Added the possibility to hide a mount in Admin Lands.

[h3]UI/UX Improvements[/h3]
[b]Fixed[/b]: The effects bar now automatically adjusts its size to fit all buffs and debuffs, expanding when new ones are added and shrinking when they are removed. 
[b]Fixed[/b]: The "Criminal" effect remains after the character's death, but the icon indicating the duration of the effect disappeared for players. The issue with the icon disappearing has been resolved.
[b]Fixed[/b]: New system messages were added for various actions.

As part of our ongoing commitment to enhancing the game, we’ve taken steps toward optimizing the game for better performance. With this update, we’ve fine-tuned the event (tick) rate to minimize packet loss, reduce bottlenecks, and improve overall open-world gameplay. 

Stay tuned for more updates, as we’ve got exciting changes and improvements on the horizon to make your experience even better!

notes.title: Life is Feudal: Arden - Patch Notes 0.27.0.26
notes.notes:
Feudals,

This patch focuses on resolving two of the most significant ongoing issues that players have been encountering over time. We’ve worked to fix these persistent problems in hopes of improving your experience in the game. Here’s a breakdown of the changes made and a preview of what to expect in the upcoming patch:

[h3]Guilds[/h3]
[b]Fixed[/b]: The “Destroy” and “Repair” abilities during Holy Judgement Hour (HJH) have been disabled.

[h3]UX Improvements[/h3]
[b]Fixed[/b]: The issue with players being stuck on the “Waiting for Server” screen (WFS error) has been resolved.
[b]Updated[/b]: We’ve made significant optimizations to the web, including updates to maps, shops, and other key areas, with essential additions and important fixes implemented. If you come across any issues or have additional feedback, don't hesitate to share it as we will continue to refine and enhance the experience for all users.

[h3]Guilds - Upcoming Changes:[/h3]
We’ve observed the emergence of T4 guilds on the server, which aligns with our initial goal of addressing guild formations. However, we’ve encountered a new challenge related to the cost of maintaining outposts for larger guilds being too low currently.

[h3]What’s Changing:[/h3]
In the upcoming patch, we will be recalculating the maintenance costs for outposts, particularly when a guild owns more than a certain number. Guilds that control up to 7 outposts will not incur any additional charges, but the costs for maintaining larger holdings could increase by 20-30 times. This adjustment aims to restore balance to the current economy.
We’ll closely monitor the impact of these changes and may also look at ways to adjust guild income, such as increasing the loot sale prices from Knools.

[b]Here's a little heads-up[/b]: gathering a bit more gold now could help keep things smooth when the changes arrive!

We’ll be keeping an eye on the results and will make any necessary adjustments. We’re also focused on addressing additional issues in upcoming patches, so keep an eye out for further improvements!

notes.title: Life is Feudal: Arden - Patch Notes 0.27.0.23
notes.notes:
Feudals,
This week’s patch brings a set of fixes aimed at resolving recent issues that have been impacting your experience in the game. Let’s dive into the update and explore the latest changes:

[h3]Outposts[/h3]
[b]Changed[/b]: The Mill outpost now divides resources based on half of its quality, with this mechanic not applying to other outposts. Other outposts will generate resources based on their quality levels.

[h3]Farming [/h3]
[b]Fixed:[/b] The "Flavour" ability has been disabled for several crop items (Onion, Green Onion, Small Onion, Carrot, Sugar Carrot, Cabbage, White Cabbage) to prevent abuse and maintain the intended planting and harvesting process.

[h3]Arena[/h3]
[b]Fixed:[/b] The issue with the DB error during transferring to the arena has been addressed, and transfers are now functioning properly.
[b]Fixed:[/b] Players will retain all items they entered the arena with.

[h3]UI/UX Improvements[/h3]
[b]Fixed: [/b]The incorrect message about the cell being leveled when skinning has been resolved, and players will now see the correct message.
[b]Fixed:[/b] A distance check has been implemented in the "Ability planning" mode to ensure that players can only interact with objects within a reasonable range. This prevents players from placing objects too far from them.
[b]Fixed:[/b] Notifications regarding player actions within the guild will now appear in the guild chat.

We hope these updates make your journey smoother, and we’ll continue working on more improvements in future patches, which will include:
[list]
[*] Improving overall stability, including the unstable behavior of individual servers (which encompasses the issue with WFS after disconnecting from servers);
[*] Introducing Instanced Battles (IBs).
[/list]
Please note that IBs were not fully enabled during the previous two days. Provinces that were already claimed will not be reset after this maintenance, and the lands will remain under the control of the guilds that captured them for a brief period. We will provide further details on this matter shortly.

Additionally, crafted totems have been removed from inventories, with resources fully refunded to those who crafted them.

Thank you for being part of the adventure - stay tuned for what's coming next!

notes.title: Life is Feudal: Arden - 0.27.0.21 patch notes
notes.notes:
[h3]Character progression[/h3]
[b]Added[/b]: Players can now change personality builds at Military Outposts.

[h3]Personal claim management[/h3]
[b]Fixed[/b]: Many “green zone” players have suffered unfair losses as other players had the ability to move the carts beyond the claim and then loot them. Now players other than the owner are no longer able to use any interactions with objects inside a personal claim.

[h3]Guilds[/h3]
[b]Fixed[/b]: Military Outposts can be now built on the server border.
[b]Changed[/b]: The “Trespassers!” ability now applies a constant 180-second criminal debuff to a player. The radius of the “Trespass” ability has also been increased from 20 to 25 tiles. Now guild members should be able to effectively protect their claim against guilds with neutral standing and non-guilded players without losing alignment. 
[b]Fixed[/b]: Certain fiefs still did not permit outpost construction (the whole territory was “red”). That happened due to several terrains overlapping. When terrains overlap on a single fief, the outpost construction will take place based on the terrain of the area to which the fief is attached. 

[h3]Outposts[/h3]
[b]Changed[/b]: The production at Mill Outposts has been rebalanced. The following items have been added to production:
[list]
[*] Big potato
[*] Grape vine
[*] Rich flax seeds
[*] White cabbage seeds
[*] Sugar carrot seeds
[*] Small onion
[*] Green peas
[*] Barley
[*] Oat
[*] Rye
[*] Wheat
[/list] The following items have been removed from production:
[list]
[*] Flour
[*] Crushed oat
[*] Rye Flour
[*] White Flour
[/list] [b]Fixed[/b]: The quality of resources produced at the mill outpost now depends on its quality, with the product quality being halved from the mill's quality (for ex. Q100 outpost production caps at q50 crops).

[h3]Forestry[/h3]
[b]Changed[/b]: We have received multiple signals from the community about the tree growth being too fast. We have made the necessary adjustments to rebalance this aspect and to decrease the speed of this process.

[h3]Farming[/h3]
[b]Changed[/b]: The production of herbs in the Large Herbal Garden has been increased by 40 per cycle. Additionally, the production cycle time has been extended to 450 minutes, equivalent to 1.56 in-game days.

[h3]Hunting[/h3]
[b]Fixed[/b]: We have finetuned the “Look for tracks of peaceful/aggressive animals” ability. Now, upon using this ability, a player will either be shown tracks of nearby animals, or they will receive a notification that no animals can be found nearby.

[h3]Crafting[/h3]
[b]Fixed[/b]: The "Mass Produce" option has been added to the Storage Box recipe in the workbench.

[h3]Arena abuse[/h3]
[b]Fixed[/b]: Players can no longer register for the arena if they are within the territory of another player's claim (a system message will appear: "You did not accept the invitation to the arena. Your request has been canceled”).

[h3]UI/UX Improvements[/h3]
[b]Fixed[/b]: The Tailors Workshop sign texture has been updated and will appear as intended.
[b]Fixed[/b]: The Stonemason's workplace UI no longer closes when shaping rock, allowing you to move out shaped rock while continuing the process.
[b]Fixed[/b]: The "Rules" button has been enabled in the world selection menu.

notes.title: Life is Feudal: Arden - Steam release date!
notes.notes:
Feudals!

The moment you’ve all been asking for is just around the corner - [b]Life is Feudal: Arden will be released on Steam on February 25, 2025![/b]

With this step, we open yet another pathway to the united world of Arden, bridging the gap for the community on the platform. Only a few days remain before countless lords and ladies can claim their rightful place as feudals of these vast expanses.🌿

On Arden, you are free to carve your own path in a world that is dynamic and constantly evolving, giving you the freedom to shape its future. Whether you choose to cultivate the land and master crafts in the "green zone", or battle fierce enemies and form powerful alliances in the "red zone" — there’s no limit to what you can achieve. Every corner of this world is yours to conquer, and how you play is entirely up to you!

We’re thrilled to offer this free-to-play experience on Steam, and we can’t wait for you to see everything that Arden has to offer. The world is waiting, get ready to leave your mark on history! ⚔️
